name: Cochin Shipyard Ltd
tagline: Shipbuilding + high-margin ship-repair growth story, but a large-cap on ~60x earnings with a weak recent quarter and thin disclosure
business_overview: Cochin Shipyard builds and repairs vessels for the Indian Navy, Coast Guard and commercial customers; ship-repair (35-40% margin) is the faster-growing, higher-margin leg vs shipbuilding (14-20% margin). New mega dry dock and ISRF commissioned; MoUs with A.P. Moller-Maersk and HD Hyundai for India shipbuilding/repair; revenue target ~Rs 12,000 Cr by FY27 vs ~Rs 4,240 Cr TTM.
fundamentals_table: ~13.3% avg; shipbuilding ~35% and ship-repair ~100%+ CAGR FY22-25 off small bases
fundamentals_narrative: Mixed. The ship-repair ramp is real and high-margin, and the FY27 Rs 12,000 Cr revenue target implies ~3x growth. But Q2 FY26 profit fell ~43% YoY with other income masking weak operations, the stock is ~40% off its ATH yet still on ~60x earnings and ~7x book, and members have flagged that the company has not published an investor presentation or concall transcript since Q1 FY25 — a disclosure-quality concern for a PSU.
technical_read: Not checked — size and valuation decisive.
sentiment_summary: Thread 'Cochin Shipyard - No more Cheap' (topic 33814, 139 posts) has gone quiet (last post Jun 2026). Bulls (contributor '1957', bias-disclosed, invested from lower levels) cite Atmanirbhar Bharat, Maritime India Vision 2047, dry-dock capacity and the Maersk/HD Hyundai MoUs. Skeptics note PSU shipyards historically have lumpy execution and thin margins, that global shipyards rarely exceed 15-20x earnings, and that CSL stopped hosting concalls/publishing decks after Q1 FY25.
community_signal: Retail-bullish, bias-disclosed, thread dormant; no core-tier trusted conviction call. Informational only.
bse_notes: Not checked. Note: no investor presentation / concall transcript published since Q1 FY25 (member-reported).

value_chain.position: Mid-tier defence + commercial shipyard; differentiated on large-vessel dry-dock + ship-repair capacity
value_chain.bottleneck_node: large-vessel dry-dock / ship-repair capacity in India (scarce)
value_chain.note: Ship-repair is the genuinely scarce, high-margin node and CSL is adding capacity there; but capacity is being added across all Indian yards, the near-term quarter was weak, and the valuation already prices the FY27 target.

bull_case: Ship-repair (35-40% margin) scaling fast off a small base; new mega dry dock + ISRF live; Rs 12,000 Cr FY27 revenue target = ~3x
Policy tailwind (Maritime India Vision, shipbuilding cluster) and marquee MoUs (Maersk, HD Hyundai)
bear_case: Large-cap (~Rs 40,400 Cr) on ~60x earnings / ~7x book despite being ~40% off ATH — no margin of safety for this screen's return bar
Q2 FY26 profit -43% YoY with operations weaker than headline; lumpy PSU execution history
No investor deck / concall since Q1 FY25 — disclosure quality has regressed
verdict_headline: Genuine ship-repair growth leg, but a richly-valued large-cap with a weak recent quarter and deteriorating disclosure
verdict_reasoning: External-lead (shipbuilding & maritime theme). Even the bullish FY27 Rs 12,000 Cr target is ~3x revenue, not 10x, and at compressed shipyard multiples off a ~Rs 40,400 Cr base the return math cannot reach this screen's bar.
Recent-quarter trend is negative (Q2 FY26 PAT -43%, other-income-supported) and disclosure has thinned — the opposite of a confirmed inflection.
Large-cap default 'neither' stands; no specific management/structural inflection strong enough to override it.

four_box.note: value_chain: 'ship-repair is the genuinely scarce, high-margin node' (tailwind=yes) but 'capacity is being added across all Indian yards' (moat weak); return math at a ~Rs40,400cr base 'cannot reach this screen's bar' (tam=no) and 'the valuation already prices the FY27 target' (valuation=no).
